IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. OF 2025  (arising out of SLP(Crl.) No. 10754/2025)
 ANIL KUMAR SHAH @ ANI SHAH ..... AP  VERSUS  STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH ..... RES
O R D E R Leave granted.
The appellant, Anil Kumar Shah @ Ani Shah, has been in custody since 01.03.2021, that is, for more than four years and seven months.
We are informed that charges were framed in the case only on 01.08.2025.
Therefore, the trial, involving examination of more than 70 listed witnesses, which is yet to commence will necessarily take a sufficiently long period of time to conclude.
The appellant, Anil Kumar Shah @ Ani Shah, is stated to have received a sum of 21.67 crores through his company from the main accused in the Bike Bot Scam.

Further, we are informed that the Directorate of Enforcement has attached Tower A in the appellants project Amadeus situated at GH-02A, Sector-143, Noida201301, Uttar Pradesh, having a value of 23,15,66,400/- (Rupees twenty three crores fifteen lakhs sixty six thousand four hundred only) as per the Valuation Report dated 23.07.2021.
We are further informed that this attachment is still subsisting and has not been lifted.
In these circumstances, we are of the opinion that the continued incarceration of the appellant, Anil Kumar Shah @ Ani Shah, is not warranted at this stage.

He shall, accordingly, be released on bail in connection with Case Crime/First Information Report No. 206/2019 dated 12.02.2019 registered with Police Station  Dadri, District  Gautam Buddh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 409, 201 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860,
on such terms and conditions as may be deemed appropriate by the trial Court.

The only exception thereto is that he may enter the National Capital Territory of Delhi as he is stated to be a resident of NOIDA.

sentences.text: We make it clear that grant of bail to the appellant would not, in any manner, affect the pending cases in relation to the other co-accused and also the main accused in the Bike Bot Scam.
No parity shall be drawn by any such accused with the appellant, Anil Kumar Shah @ Ani Shah, for seeking bail, as each case would have to be decided on its own merits.

Given the fact that the charges were framed on 01.08.2025 and the matter involves the interests of more than 2,46,462 investors, we would request the Special Court which is seized of the matter to take up the trial of the case on a day-to-day basis to the extent possible.
The appeal is, accordingly, allowed, setting aside the impugned order dated 28.05.2025 passed by the High Court.
We clarify that we have not made any observations/comments on the merits of the case and any observation made in this order is meant only for the limited purpose of grant of bail.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
